notes.title: A lantern at dusk
notes.body: The party is resting at the Three Kettles inn in the village of Ashford when the miller, Odra, bursts in.
notes.dmNotes: Let each player introduce their character in one sentence: who they are and why they care about the village.

scene.readAloud: The door slams open. A flour-dusted woman grips the frame, out of breath. "My boy Pell went to fetch our dog at the old mill. That was hours ago, and now there's a strange green lantern moving in the mill yard. Please. Night is coming."
scene.triggers: The players ask Odra questions or agree to help.
scene.outcomes: Odra gives directions and her spare lantern. If asked, she remembers hearing high, cackling voices near the mill last night.
scene.rewards: Odra offers 10 GP and free bread for a month.

notes.title: Odra, the miller
notes.body: A practical, tired widow who runs the new mill by the river. Worried sick about her son Pell (10) and their old dog, Biscuit.
notes.dmNotes: Odra sold the old mill last winter and suspects the buyer, but she won't say so unless a character earns her trust (a Charisma (Persuasion) check, DC 12).

notes.title: Find Pell before nightfall
notes.body: Pell went to the old mill to fetch the family dog and has not come back. A green lantern moves in the mill yard.
notes.dmNotes: The goblins were paid by the new owner of the old mill to scare villagers away. Pell is hiding, unharmed, in the grain loft with Biscuit.

notes.title: The old mill
notes.body: A crooked stone mill with a broken waterwheel, a muddy yard and a grain loft reached by a rotten ladder.
notes.dmNotes: Searching the yard (Wisdom (Perception), DC 10) reveals small footprints leading to the loft and larger, clawed ones by the door. On a success, the characters are not surprised by the goblins.

scene.readAloud: Mist rolls off the river. In the yard, a green lantern swings from a pole, and two small figures crouch behind the woodpile, giggling.
scene.triggers: The characters enter the yard or call out.
scene.outcomes: Two goblins attack. If one falls, the other flees toward the woods. Pell calls out from the loft once the fighting stops.
scene.rewards: Pell and Biscuit return home; Odra pays the reward. Each character gains one milestone level if this was their first adventure.

encounter.name: Trouble at Ashford Mill
encounter.notes: Two goblins behind the woodpile. Easy for two level 1 characters; let the players learn the turn order, the action bar and the dice.

dm.title: Invite your players
dm.body: Open the Invites section of this room and share a code. Each player makes a character with a motivation and a bond to the party.

dm.title: Read the hook
dm.body: Open the story notes and read "A lantern at dusk" aloud. The quest and NPC are already shared with the players; your notes stay private.

dm.title: Ask for a check
dm.body: At the mill, ask for a Wisdom (Perception) check, DC 10. Players roll a d20 and add their modifier in the dice tray.

dm.title: Run the tutorial combat
dm.body: On the Combat page, prepare "Trouble at Ashford Mill" on the map "Ashford Mill yard", add the characters, set initiative and begin.

dm.title: Change the encounter if you like
dm.body: Add or remove monsters or pick a different difficulty in the encounter builder. The tutorial never locks anything.

dm.title: Reward and progression
dm.body: Give the reward from the scene notes. Grant a milestone level from each character sheet.

dm.title: Write the recap
dm.body: Start a session on the Session page and write a short recap for the party. It saves by itself.

player.title: Make your character
player.body: Choose a concept, a motivation and a bond to the party in the character wizard.

player.title: Read the quest
player.body: Your DM shares the quest and the people you meet in the story notes.

player.title: Roll a check
player.body: When the DM asks for a check, roll a d20 in the dice tray and add your modifier.

player.title: Take your turn
player.body: In combat, pick an action from the action bar, choose a target and take the action. The DM decides the effects.
